item.title: Stop asking AI to be creative. Ask it to be correct

Fast Company's post says we should ask AI to be accurate, not creative. With so many tasks still mundane, freeing up time for human-led work gives better results. The caution: the change might require a mind shift, especially in industries leaning on creativity.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: AI skills are entering performance reviews. Are managers ready?
item.description:
AI skills are creeping into reviews, but not everyone is ready. HiBob found that while AI is impacting promotions and pay, managers and systems might not be up to speed. This insight is based on one company's research, so it might not reflect all industries.
— via Charter

item.title: How Extreme Heat Affects the Economy
item.description:
Extreme heat can hurt productivity, says Professor R. Jisung Park. Even academic success isn't spared. But this is premium research tying deep climate trends to work outcomes, meaning it’s not yet actionable for daily HR tasks.
— via Knowledge at Wharton

item.title: The Impact of Deep Care Isa on Reducing Musculoskeletal Disorders and Enhancing Productivity Among Office Employees: A Comprehensive Study
item.description:
Deep Care Isa could help office workers move more and ache less. A study showed improvements in ergonomic practices and less sick leave. However, be aware it focuses on office settings and might not fit other work environments.
— via arXiv

item.title: Novartis’s Christian Diehl on scaling AI beyond the demo
item.description:
Novartis is scaling AI beyond demos, says their digital lead. They see benefits in safety and speed for research. Note it’s a company view without peer review, making broad lessons tentative.
— via McKinsey

item.title: Does AI Save Time on Product Design? A Randomized Controlled Experiment of AI Prompt-to-Design Workflows
item.description:
A trial found that AI could save time in product design. It tested out Figma Make in a real setting, showing promising speed-ups. But results came from a small sample, so broader impacts aren't guaranteed.
— via arXiv

item.title: 15 Best Global HR Certifications To Enroll In [2026 Edition]
item.description:
Deciding on global HR certifications? AIHR lists 15 top options. With more roles going international, picking the right training is crucial. Keep in mind it's a vendor’s list, not an independent rating.
— via AIHR

item.title: Stepping into the Margins: How Readers Want AI to Generate Footnotes
item.description:
People want AI to help with footnotes in texts. It's about enhancing understanding but current tools still lack personal touch. This is academic research, not yet a workplace tool.
— via arXiv

item.title: 5 things to know about required minimum distributions in 2026
item.description:
RMD age changes are in play, affecting taxes for retirees. It could save dollars, but impacts are specific to retirees. It's crucial for those on the edge of retirement, skipping younger workers altogether.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: Jatin Suley joins Varroc as cluster head HR
item.description:
Jatin Suley's move to Varroc as HR head adds industry depth. He brings decades of experience spanning several major sectors. Announcements like this offer insights but little direct action for most HR teams.
— via HR Katha

item.title: International Day of Peace: How HR Can Build Peace at Work
item.description:
A piece on building peace at work highlights how inclusive HR policies foster unity. It shows that programs like refugee employment can create environments of dignity. However, it’s built on examples that might not be scalable for smaller companies.
— via HRD Connect

item.title: Colorado judge: Doctor’s burnout wasn’t a disability
item.description:
A Colorado court ruled that burnout doesn't qualify as a disability under ADA. This decision clarifies some boundaries of what counts legally as a disability. But, it's specific to one state, and different jurisdictions may interpret things differently.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Want a promotion? Your performance counts but your behavior counts more
item.description:
A piece in Fast Company emphasizes that behavior, rather than performance alone, can drive promotions. This surprises those who believe results speak for themselves. However, it draws from anecdotes rather than comprehensive research.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: Equity Can Motivate Frontline Employees—If They See Their Impact on the Bottom Line
item.description:
New research says frontline employees get a boost if they see how equity affects the bottom line. This visibility can tie their everyday efforts to a company’s success, increasing motivation. But, it's all based on selective cases, so the broader application remains to be seen.
— via HBR

item.title: Why experts need to embrace the beginners mindset
item.description:
Experts adopting a beginner's mindset can reskill effectively by embracing the unknown. It helps them regain a sense of competence in new areas, which is crucial for growth. The challenge is that feeling safe in 'beginnerhood' can be tough for experienced workers to accept.
— via HRZone

item.title: Research: The True Cost of Corporate Scandals? Talent.
item.description:
HBR spotlights how corporate scandals inflict long-term damage by driving away talent. Leaders need to keep their reputation clean to avoid the costly fallout of a talent exodus. This is based on specific cases, so it doesn't account for all industries or business sizes.
— via HBR

item.title: How employers can make good decisions about remote work before the next crisis strikes
item.description:
Guidance on remote work emphasizes planning for the next crisis rather than reacting. Having a framework can smooth out the shift and keep operations fluid. But the right approach varies widely, and there's no one-size-fits-all formula.
— via The Conversation Business

item.title: WidgetVA: A Widget-Centric Framework and Benchmark for Agentic Visual Analytics
item.description:
A new framework called WidgetVA aims to use AI to make visual data analysis smoother. It could take over some complex tasks of observing and interpreting data. However, this is still academic and not ready for prime-time use in the business world.
— via arXiv

item.title: WIRED: The AI playbook top companies use
item.description:
McKinsey’s new playbook claims companies need fundamental changes to reach AI’s full potential. This involves rewiring tech and leadership practices for better outcomes. But, it leans heavily on McKinsey's own insights and might be more aspirational than practical for now.
— via McKinsey

item.title: Teen’s ‘therapeutic’ DJ classes did not entitle mother to FMLA leave, court finds
item.description:
A recent court decision says taking leave to attend a child's therapeutic classes doesn't qualify under FMLA. This decision sharpens the understanding of what constitutes FMLA-eligible activities. Yet, it's a single case with limited jurisdiction scope.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Passthrough Rigidity: The Behavioral and Visuomotor Costs of Mediated Perception
item.description:
Researchers analyze why head-mounted displays remain uncomfortable despite tech upgrades. They delve into how users perceive mediated interaction and its effects. The results come from a study with a specific setup, not directly applicable to all contexts.
— via arXiv

item.title: onPanda: Efficient Annotation of On-Policy Alignment Data for LLMs and Agents via Token-Level Correction
item.description:
onPanda offers a new way to correct AI by editing its outputs token by token. It promises a more efficient means to fine-tune AI responses. But, the study is small-scale, and the tool is still in its ideation stage.
— via arXiv

item.title: Despite the hype, innovation isn’t getting any faster. Here’s why
item.description:
Despite constant chatter, innovation isn't speeding up, according to a Fast Company post. Productivity figures don't show a faster pace compared to past decades. Yet, this conclusion draws from selective statistical interpretations, not universal truths.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: Managerial augmentation vs managerial substitution: When technology helps managers and when it replaces them
item.description:
A discussion on managerial roles points out how technology can both aid and replace managers. It’s about determining when tech helps versus when it substitutes. The catch is understanding these dynamics may require more than just reading a quick article.
— via HR Katha

item.title: How to build psychological safety into recruitment
item.description:
Helen Sanderson at HRZone dives into how psychological safety can be baked into recruitment. It's about making candidates feel safe to truly showcase their potential in interviews. Keep in mind: this is part two of a series, so it builds on previous advice that you may need to catch up on.
— via HRZone

item.title: The AI-era utility workforce paradox: Aging fast while growing faster
item.description:
Deloitte highlights a paradox in the utilities sector: it's growing with AI but workers are aging fast. This means you'll need a strategy for both attracting young talent and keeping older workers skilled. The catch: it's a complex picture reliant on industry-specific data.
— via Deloitte

item.title: Beyonce's former strategist on turning employees into fans
item.description:
A piece from Charter explores how to turn employees into fans, inspired by Beyonce's strategist. It’s about creating a company culture that employees are genuinely excited about. Remember, not all employees resonate with celebrity fan culture, so tailor it to your audience.
— via Charter

item.title: UK vacancies fall to lowest non-pandemic level since 2014 as recovery remains uncertain
item.description:
Onrec reveals that UK vacancies have dropped to the lowest level since 2014 outside of the pandemic. This means hiring could become more competitive as fewer jobs are available. But mixed signals from recruitment surveys suggest this trend is still uncertain.
— via Onrec

item.title: Two's a Crowd: Human and AI-Based Copresence for Developers with ADHD
item.description:
A study explores how AI assistance and human collaboration can aid developers with ADHD. This might boost productivity and focus in hybrid work settings. The limitation: it focuses on a specific group—developers with ADHD, which might not directly map to all teams.
— via arXiv

item.title: When AI Enters the Workplace, Who Faces Greater Risks? A Gendered Analysis
item.description:
New research looks at AI's impact on gender disparities in the workplace. Women may be at greater risk of being left behind unless upskilling measures are taken. The focus here is specific to gender, so additional factors could also be at play.
— via arXiv

item.title: A Sociotechnical Review of Algorithms in Health Systems: Technical, Cost, and Human-Centered Considerations
item.description:
A review from arXiv examines how AI models are shaping healthcare. It suggests these tools can reduce costs but come with hidden layers of complexity. This analysis is technical-heavy, especially relevant to those in health sectors.
— via arXiv

item.title: Apple trims jobs amid cost pressures
item.description:
HR Katha reports on Apple's recent job cuts in the Fitness+ division. It serves as a reminder of ongoing corporate restructuring amid financial pressures. Note that while Apple sets trends, each firm operates under different circumstances which affect applicability.
— via HR Katha

item.title: Everyone Gets the Same Models. The Edge Is Your Workforce.
item.description:
A BCG piece states that every company can access the same AI models, but people give you an edge. It's a reminder to invest in your workforce to stand out. Be aware that it's from a consultancy, so the advice may be promotional.
— via BCG

item.title: How to end a client relationship on good terms
item.description:
Fast Company gives advice on ending client relationships respectfully. Knowing when to walk away can save your team's energy and morale. It's aimed at those managing external business but still offers insights for internal alignment.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: Ignoring a doctor’s note can be costly, EEOC reminds employers
item.description:
HR Dive covers a reminder from the EEOC about respecting doctor's notes, especially for pregnancies. Ignoring them can lead to costly discrimination claims. This is U.S.-centric advice, which international firms should adapt with local laws in mind.
— via HR Dive

item.title: How to figure out which advice is worth taking
item.description:
Fast Company discusses how to filter out worthwhile advice from noise. It's about being selective to boost personal and team productivity. Use this sparingly; not all advice fits every organizational context.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: Employers may not know how to explain their pay decisions, Aon says
item.description:
A report from HR Dive suggests plenty of firms aren't clear on explaining why they pay what they do. With pay transparency laws in place, this clarity is crucial. But, remember, the findings are based on a survey, which may not cover all industries.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Case study: What I learned from leading a team through administration
item.description:
An HRZone case study shares leadership lessons from guiding a company through administration. It’s a firsthand account of building resilience during tough times. The insights stem from a specific industry, so consider broader applications.
— via HRZone

item.title: Here’s why some US industrial companies achieve higher multiples
item.description:
McKinsey highlights how select US industrial companies get higher valuations. They combine specific management actions that set them apart from competitors. But remember, this is one perspective that's most useful for those in similar markets.
— via McKinsey

item.title: McKinsey Technology Trends Outlook 2026
item.description:
McKinsey's 2026 Technology Trends Outlook covers the tech that will matter most. This impacts talent strategies as companies adjust to new technology needs. Yet, it's a broad analysis; your industry specifics could differ.
— via McKinsey

item.title: When to Buy Your Next Recruiter and When to Build One: A Framework for Recruitment Firm Owners
item.description:
Onrec explains when to hire a seasoned recruiter and when to train from scratch. It's about your capacity to provide initial workload and time for coaching. Plan carefully: it hinges on your current workload and time availability.
— via Onrec

item.title: What Leaders Need to Know About AI and Psychological Safety ^ H09B95
item.description:
HBR shares insights on how AI affects psychological safety in teams. AI’s role can impact trust and communication among team members, making psychological safety vital. However, examples might be more relevant to those who already use AI.
— via HBR

item.title: FenceXR: AR Movement Replay for Error-Detection Training and Spatially Grounded Feedback
item.description:
FenceXR offers AR-based feedback for complex sports training. It's designed to spotlight technical errors with spatial feedback, enhancing motor skills learning. But keep in mind, this applies mainly to sports training scenarios for now.
— via arXiv

item.title: Stereotypically Yours: Portrayal and Perception of Race-Coded AI Companions
item.description:
A study on AI companions reveals biases in how racial personas are perceived. These biases indicate the influence of user expectations on interaction with AI. Consider that findings are limited by a small participant size and specific interactions.
— via arXiv

item.title: TeamCAMS: An Open-Source Research Platform for Studying Human Behaviour in Human-AI Teams
item.description:
An open-source platform, TeamCAMS, aids research on human-AI interaction. It's crucial for understanding team dynamics in AI-supported tasks. However, it's primarily a research tool, so practical implications may vary.
— via arXiv

item.title: Amazon ups minimum hourly starting wage to $20
item.description:
Amazon raises its minimum hourly wage to $20 for certain full-time roles. This move increases competition for talent and pushes other companies to rethink pay structures. It's specific to Amazon's operations and industries with similar dynamics.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Recruitment Spotlight: Hightekers on Freelance Freedom Without Sacrificing Security
item.description:
Hightekers talks about balancing freelance freedom with job security. It's key for agencies looking to recruit flexible yet dedicated talent. Yet, it’s a narrower fit for those already in boutique niches or familiar with hybrid models.
— via Onrec

item.title: I use AI to save time. So why am I working more?
item.description:
A personal account reveals how AI can both save time and increase workload. The integration of AI might lead to expanding responsibilities beyond initial expectations. Bear in mind, individual outcomes will vary widely.
— via Fast Company Work Life
